## 0. Imported inputs, standard theorems, and what is proved here

**Verified dependency.** ATT-0065 (subproblem C66-GEO-Z), independently confirmed by REV-0108 (pass 1) and REV-0109 (pass 2). I use: CLM-0065-1 (under the two degree inequalities, pi_*W and pi_*(W|Gamma) are locally free of the stated ranks with arbitrary base change, and Fit_0(coker phi)=I_{2n}(phi)); CLM-0065-3 (filtered snake reduction coker(phi)=coker(phi_5)=R^1pi_*(W_5(-Gamma)), with no global splitting of W); CLM-0065-4 (Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e over arbitrary locally Noetherian bases, compatible with arbitrary base change, with the rigidified T-point criterion N_T=pi_T^*M_T and smooth-atlas descent); CLM-0065-5 (fibrewise balanced F yields the canonical O(5)-subbundle, hence the filtration 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 with fibre degrees 20 and 16 at g=6); CLM-0065-9 (the balanced (6,6) specialization: ranks 26->12 and the failure scheme equal to the relative incidence O_C(Gamma)=W_5 tensor omega^{-1}). Nothing else is imported from ATT-0065, and none of its ambient equation-bundle hypotheses are needed below.

**Source-backed inputs.** SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6, as excerpted in the packet: the CE convention W_f=(O_X(2) tensor gamma^*O(-f))|_C with the essential minus sign, the degree formula deg(W_f|_C)=4g+12-4f, and the underlying deg(O_X(1)|_C)=2g-2+4*2, i.e. 18 at g=6.

**Standard theorems used without reproof.** Riemann-Roch and Serre duality on smooth projective curves; Clifford's theorem for special effective divisors together with its equality cases (D=0, D=K, or C hyperelliptic with D a multiple of the g^1_2); Grauert's criterion (constant fibre dimension over a REDUCED base gives local freeness and base change); relative duality for a smooth proper relative curve; the fact that a closed immersion between two schemes smooth over a common base is a regular immersion with locally free conormal sheaf and locally split conormal sequence; representability of Sym^d(C/S) and its identification with the functor of relative effective Cartier divisors on a smooth relative curve; the classical description of the fibre of the Abel-Jacobi morphism and of its differential.

**Not used.** No finite computation, no numerical experiment, no database, no web-sourced claim, and no packet finding is used as a proof step: where a packet adjudicated finding says the same thing as a step below, the step is nevertheless proved here from the listed standard inputs. In particular the (6,6) degree table is re-derived rather than quoted.

**Relation to other campaign artifacts.** The primary working context lists 'Nonemptiness of the reduced-support open in |L_b| and of the ordered Conf_6 incidence on every balanced geometric fibre' as an open frontier obligation, and the archive overflow lists both the local commutative-algebra (minimal generators, depth, conormal rank, regular sequence) verification of the lci property of Z and the constancy of the relative dimension 2 over all of balanced tetragonal moduli. Those are the items this artifact attacks. The repository tree contains further attempts and reviews touching these questions; none of them is a verified dependency of TASK-C66-M-008, so none is cited or relied on, and every statement below is proved from scratch.

## 1. Setup, and the twist ambiguity of W_5 and L

Keep the notation of the theorem. On P=P_S(V) the relative O_P(1) is determined only up to twist by s^*(line bundle on S); consequently W_4, W_5, L=W_5 tensor omega^{-1} and D=gamma^*O_P(1) are determined only up to tensoring by pi^*(line bundle on S). Every object used below is invariant under such a twist: projectivizations P_S(pi_*L) are unchanged when L is twisted from the base; the incidence condition 'O(Gamma) is isomorphic to L tensor pi^*M for some invertible M on the base' is unchanged; and Fitting ideals are invariant under an invertible twist of the evaluation map (ATT-0065, CLM-0065-4). Fibrewise the ambiguity disappears altogether. All statements are therefore well posed; this is the discipline demanded by the working-context constraint on quantifying W_5 or L over a family rather than over geometric fibres, and no global splitting of F or of W is ever used: only the canonical filtration of CLM-0065-5.

Throughout, a geometric fibre means the data (C,gamma,E,F,X,W,L,D) over a geometric point of S, with C smooth projective connected of genus 6 and gamma finite flat of degree 4 onto P1.

## 2. Part (I.1): the normalization forces A trivial, so L=omega_C(-D)

By SRC-0004, deg(O_X(1)|_C)=2g-2+4*2=10+8=18. Hypothesis (N) gives O_X(1)|_C = omega_{C/P1} tensor gamma^*A = omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2) tensor gamma^*A, of degree 10+8+4deg(A)=18+4deg(A) since gamma has degree 4. Comparing, deg(A)=0, and Pic(P1)=Z forces A trivial. Hence O_X(1)|_C = omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2), and therefore

  W_5 = (O_X(2) tensor gamma^*O(-5))|_C = omega_C^2 tensor gamma^*O(4) tensor gamma^*O(-5) = omega_C^2(-D),
  W_4 = (O_X(2) tensor gamma^*O(-4))|_C = omega_C^2,
  L = W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} = omega_C(-D).

Degrees: deg(W_4)=20 and deg(W_5)=16, matching 4g+12-4f at g=6 and f=4,5; deg(L)=16-10=6; and Riemann-Roch gives chi(L)=6-6+1=1. This proves (I.1). Note that (N) is used only here; Sections 3 and 8 do not use it.

## 3. Part (I.2): (CE) and (BAL) force C non-hyperelliptic

Suppose C is hyperelliptic with hyperelliptic map h:C->P1 of degree 2.

*Step 1: gamma factors through h.* Consider (h,gamma):C->P1 x P1. If it were birational onto its image Y, then with Y of class a({pt} x P1)+b(P1 x {pt}) one has deg(pr_1|_Y)=b and deg(pr_2|_Y)=a, so b=2 and a=4; the arithmetic genus of a curve of bidegree (4,2) is (4-1)(2-1)=3, and the geometric genus of Y is then at most 3, contradicting that C, of genus 6, maps birationally onto Y. Hence (h,gamma) has degree at least 2 onto its image. Since h has degree 2, the map (h,gamma) has degree exactly 2 and its image is the graph of a morphism q:P1->P1 with gamma=q o h; comparing degrees, deg(q)=2.

*Step 2: the Tschirnhausen bundle.* For a hyperelliptic curve of genus 6, h_*O_C = O direct-sum O(-7), since the branch divisor has degree 2g+2=14. For a degree-two morphism q:P1->P1, after a coordinate change q is z=x^2 and q_*O_{P1}(m) = O(floor(m/2)) direct-sum O(floor((m-1)/2)); in particular q_*O = O direct-sum O(-1) and q_*O(-7)=O(-4) direct-sum O(-4) (the Euler characteristics match: chi(O(-7))=-6=chi(O(-4) direct-sum O(-4))). Hence gamma_*O_C = O direct-sum O(-1) direct-sum O(-4) direct-sum O(-4), so E^vee = O(-1) direct-sum O(-4)^2 and E = O(1) direct-sum O(4)^2, of degree 9.

*Step 3: the CE quadric sequence.* Tensor the resolution (CE) by O_X(2):

  0 -> O_X(-2) tensor p^*det(F) -> p^*F -> I_C(2) -> 0.

On the P2-fibres H^i(P2,O(-2))=0 for i=0,1,2, so Rp_*(O_X(-2) tensor p^*det F)=0 in every degree and the projection formula gives Rp_*(I_C(2)) = F concentrated in degree zero. Since H^{>0}(P2,O(2))=0 and p_*O_X(2)=Sym^2 E in the packet convention p_*O_X(1)=E, applying Rp_* to 0 -> I_C(2) -> O_X(2) -> i_*(O_X(2)|_C) -> 0 yields the exact sequence on P1

  0 -> F -> Sym^2 E -> gamma_*(O_X(2)|_C) -> 0.

(This is the same mechanism as ATT-0065 Section 8 with a different twist; it is redone here because ATT-0065 states it only after tensoring by O_X(2) tensor p^*F^vee.)

*Step 4: section count.* Twist by O(-6) and use the projection formula: gamma_*(O_X(2)|_C) tensor O(-6) = gamma_*(W_6) with W_6=(O_X(2) tensor gamma^*O(-6))|_C of degree 2*18-24=12>2g-2=10, so h^0(C,W_6)=12-6+1=7. With E=O(1) direct-sum O(4)^2 one has Sym^2 E = O(2) direct-sum O(5)^2 direct-sum O(8)^3, so Sym^2E(-6)=O(-4) direct-sum O(-1)^2 direct-sum O(2)^3 and h^0(Sym^2E(-6))=9. Left-exactness of global sections in the twisted sequence gives h^0(F(-6)) >= 9-7 = 2. But (BAL) gives F(-6)=O(-2) direct-sum O(-1), with h^0=0. Contradiction. Hence C is not hyperelliptic, proving (I.2).

This argument does not use (N), and it makes no claim about tetragonal pencils factoring through degree-two maps onto curves of positive genus: none is needed, and none is asserted.

## 4. Part (I.3): h^0(D)=2 and h^0(L)=3, with no jumping

D=gamma^*O_P(1) is effective of degree 4 and gamma^* is injective on H^0(P1,O(1)), so h^0(O_C(D)) >= 2. By (I.1), omega_C tensor O_C(-D)=L, so Riemann-Roch h^0(D)-h^0(K-D)=4-6+1=-1 reads

  h^0(L) = h^0(O_C(D)) + 1.

Since chi(L)=1 we get h^0(L)>=1, hence h^1(D)=h^0(K-D)=h^0(L)>0 and D is special. Clifford's theorem gives h^0(D)-1 <= deg(D)/2 = 2, so h^0(D) <= 3, with equality only if D=0, D=K, or C is hyperelliptic and D is a multiple of the hyperelliptic pencil. The first two are excluded by deg(D)=4 not in {0,10}, the third by (I.2). Therefore h^0(D)=2, h^0(L)=3, and h^1(L)=h^0(L)-chi(L)=2. In particular |L| is a projective plane, and the value 3 is attained on every balanced fibre satisfying (N), i.e. h^0(L) does not jump on the balanced locus.

Finally, by the projection formula h^0(C,D)=h^0(P1,O(1) tensor gamma_*O_C)=h^0(O(1))+h^0(E^vee(1))=2+h^0(E^vee(1)); hence h^0(E^vee(1))=0 and every summand of E has degree at least two. This completes (I.3).

*Remark on a recorded constraint.* The working context blocks the assertion that constancy of h^0(omega_C(-D)) on the balanced locus is EQUIVALENT to excluding every non-primitive degree-four pencil, on the ground that the h^0(D)=3 case detects only composition with the hyperelliptic map. The argument above uses exactly that correct direction: Clifford equality is possible only in the hyperelliptic case, which balancedness kills, and no statement about factorizations through intermediate curves of genus 1, 2 or 3 is made or needed.

## 5. Part (I.4): the fixed part of |L| has degree at most one

Write |L| = B_L + |A| where B_L is the fixed part (the largest divisor contained in every member) and A=L(-B_L) is base-point-free with h^0(A)=h^0(L)=3 and deg(A)=6-b, b=deg(B_L). Suppose b>=2, so deg(A)<=4. Then chi(A)=deg(A)-5 <= -1, hence h^1(A)=h^0(A)-chi(A) >= 4 > 0 and A is special. Clifford gives 2=h^0(A)-1 <= deg(A)/2 <= 2, so deg(A)=4 and equality holds in Clifford; degrees exclude A=O_C and A=omega_C, so C would be hyperelliptic, contradicting (I.2). Hence b <= 1. In particular B_L is either zero or a single reduced point, and A is base-point-free of degree 5 or 6 with exactly three sections. This proves (I.4).

This is the step that makes the whole of Part (I) independent of base-point-freeness of L: nothing below asserts or denies that base points occur on the balanced locus.

## 6. Part (I.5), existence: |L| contains a reduced divisor

Let A be as in Section 5 and psi:C->P2 the morphism defined by the base-point-free A; it is non-degenerate because h^0(A)=3, and non-constant. Consider

  J = {(q,[t]) in C x |A| : t lies in H^0(A(-2q))},

a closed subscheme of C x |A| (it is the locus where the 2-jet evaluation H^0(A) -> A tensor O_C/m_q^2 kills t). Since A is base-point-free, the 2-jet map has rank at least 1 at every q, so h^0(A(-2q)) <= 2 and the fibre of J over q is a projective space of dimension at most 1. Let R be the closed locus of q where the 2-jet map has rank exactly 1, equivalently where d(psi)_q=0. If R were all of C then d(psi) would vanish identically and psi would be constant in characteristic zero, contradicting non-degeneracy; hence R is a proper closed subset of the irreducible curve C, i.e. finite. Therefore J is the union of a part lying over C minus R with zero-dimensional fibres, of dimension at most 1, and a part lying over the finite set R with fibres of dimension at most 1, again of dimension at most 1. So dim(J) <= 1, and since C is proper the image pr_2(J) is closed in |A| of dimension at most 1 < 2.

Hence the complement of pr_2(J) in |A| is a nonempty dense open subset, and every member of |A| in that complement has multiplicity at most 1 at every point, i.e. is a reduced divisor of deg(A) distinct points. If moreover b=1, say B_L={pt}, then the members of |A| passing through that point form a hyperplane in |A| (proper, because A is base-point-free, so h^0(A(-pt))=2<3). Removing that hyperplane as well, a general member of |A| is reduced and avoids B_L, so B_L + (that member) is a reduced divisor of |L| with six pairwise distinct points. Thus |L|^red is nonempty.

## 7. Part (I.5), dimension of the discriminant, and Part (I.6)

For every q in C, imposing vanishing to order 2 at q is at most two linear conditions on the three-dimensional H^0(L), so h^0(L(-2q)) >= 1 and |L| contains a member non-reduced at q. Hence the incidence J_L = {(q,[t]) in C x |L| : t in H^0(L(-2q))} surjects onto C with nonempty fibres, so dim(J_L) >= 1; the same fibre-dimension analysis as in Section 6 (applied to the moving part, plus the hyperplane coming from B_L when b=1) gives dim(J_L) <= 1. A member of |L| has degree 6, so at most three points of multiplicity at least 2; thus pr_2:J_L->|L| has finite fibres and Delta:=pr_2(J_L), the non-reduced locus, is closed of dimension exactly 1. In particular Delta is a nonempty proper closed subset of the irreducible surface |L|, so |L|^red=|L| minus Delta is a nonempty dense open subset of dimension 2 which is not closed in |L|. (No non-closedness statement about any locus inside M_{6,6} is made or implied; this is the fibrewise statement only.)

For (I.6): over |L|^red the universal divisor is reduced with six distinct points, so the space of orderings is a finite etale cover of degree 720 on which S_6 acts freely and transitively on fibres, i.e. a finite etale S_6-torsor. Its total space is therefore smooth of pure dimension 2 and nonempty, and it is precisely the ordered incidence {(p_1,...,p_6) pairwise distinct with sum in |L|}. This proves (I.6), and with it the frontier item on fibrewise nonemptiness of the reduced-support open and of the ordered Conf_6 incidence, for every balanced geometric fibre satisfying (N).

## 8. Part (II): rank strata and the complete minor-ideal table

Take B=Conf_6(C/S) with its six tautological pairwise-disjoint sections and universal divisor Gamma; this is exactly the situation in which the ATT-0065 hypotheses hold (Gamma a sum of n=6 pairwise disjoint sections), and no claim is made for an arbitrary relative degree-six divisor. By (I.1) the fibre degrees are d_4=20 and d_5=16 with d_4-n=14>2g-2=10 and d_5-n=10=2g-2, so CLM-0065-1 applies: R^1pi_*W=0, pi_*W is locally free of rank d_4+d_5+2-2g=20+16+2-12=26 with arbitrary base change, pi_*(W|Gamma) is locally free of rank 2n=12, and Fit_0(coker phi)=I_12(phi).

By CLM-0065-3, coker(phi)=coker(phi_5)=R^1pi_*(W_5(-Gamma)) canonically, with no global splitting used; the vanishings R^1pi_*W_4=0 and R^1pi_*(W_4(-Gamma))=0 are exactly the two degree inequalities just checked. Cokernels commute with base change, and R^1 of a relative curve commutes with arbitrary base change, so the geometric fibre of coker(phi) at a point is H^1(W_5(-Gamma)), which by Serre duality has dimension h^0(omega_C tensor W_5^vee(Gamma)). That line bundle has degree 10-16+6=0, and a degree-zero line bundle on a smooth projective connected curve has a nonzero section if and only if it is trivial (this uses effectivity of the divisor of a section, not duality; duality is used only for the identification of h^1 with an h^0). Hence the fibrewise corank is 0 or 1 and every geometric fibre of phi has rank 11 or 12.

Therefore the closed subscheme cut out by I_11(phi) has empty support, so I_11(phi)=O_B; since the minor ideals decrease, I_j(phi)=O_B for every j<=11. By CLM-0065-4 and CLM-0065-9, I_12(phi)=Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e, with formation commuting with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change, cutting out Z=a_N^{-1}(e(B)); its T-points are the T-points of B for which O(Gamma_T) is isomorphic to L_T tensor pi^*M_T for some invertible M_T on T. This proves (II.1).

For (II.2): a map of bundles of ranks 26 and 12 has generic determinantal expectation (26-11)(12-11)=15 for the corank-one locus; the filtered evaluation phi_5 has ranks 11 and 6, with expectation (11-5)(6-5)=6. The fibres of B->S are Conf_6 of a curve, of dimension 6, and by (I.6) the fibres of Z->S have pure dimension 2, i.e. codimension 4. The excess relative to the correct (filtered) expectation is 6-4=2, which equals h^1(L)=2 by (I.3). None of these numbers is used below to infer any regularity, depth, lci or Gysin statement; they are recorded as bookkeeping only.

## 9. Part (III): the projective-bundle model and smoothness of Z over S

Assume S reduced. By (I.3) the function s -> h^0(L_s) is constant equal to 3, so Grauert applies (working smooth-locally on S where a representative of L is chosen; the choice matters only up to a twist from the base, which does not affect projectivization): pi_*L is locally free of rank 3, R^1pi_*L is locally free of rank 2, and both commute with base change. Set AJ:=P_S(pi_*L), the projective bundle of line subbundles, a Zariski-locally trivial P2-bundle, smooth and proper over S of relative dimension 2. The tautological inclusion gives a canonical relative effective Cartier divisor D_univ in C x_S AJ of degree 6 with O(D_univ)=L tensor pi^*M_univ, and for a scheme T over S the T-points of AJ are exactly the relative degree-six divisors Gamma with O(Gamma) isomorphic to L_T tensor pi^*M for some invertible M on T (given such a Gamma, its canonical section defines a line subbundle of pi_*L_T because it is fibrewise nonzero). Fibrewise, AJ_s = |L_s| as a scheme, by base change.

Let U be the open subscheme of AJ over which D_univ is etale, i.e. has pairwise distinct support. Fibrewise U_s = |L_s|^red, which by Section 7 is a nonempty dense open of |L_s|; hence U->S is smooth of pure relative dimension 2 and surjective. Let Ord(U) be the scheme of orderings of D_univ|_U, i.e. of isomorphisms from the constant set {1,...,6} to D_univ|_U over U; it is a finite etale S_6-torsor over U of degree 720, hence smooth over S of pure relative dimension 2 and surjective onto S. Note that this construction applies the reduced-support condition and the ordering to the SAME scheme, with no reduction taken on either side, as the working context requires.

Comparing functors of points, Ord(U)(T) is the set of six pairwise-disjoint sections whose sum Gamma satisfies O(Gamma) isomorphic to L_T tensor pi^*M, which is exactly Z(T) by the T-point criterion in (II.1). Hence Z is canonically isomorphic to Ord(U) as an S-scheme. Consequently Z->S is smooth and surjective of pure relative dimension 2, proving the first half of (III.1). Since Z->S is flat of finite presentation, going-down shows that the generic point of every irreducible component of Z maps to a generic point of a component of S; if S is of finite type over k, the dimension formula for flat finite-type morphisms with two-dimensional fibres gives dim(component of Z) = dim(dominated component of S)+2, and likewise for U. This is the statement whose only missing input, in the recorded constraints, was fibrewise nonemptiness of the reduced-support open; that input is now supplied by Section 6. No conclusion is drawn about the dimension, closure or codimension of any image in M_{6,6}.

## 10. Part (III.2): the immersion Z -> B is regular of codimension four

Z is closed in B, being cut out by the Fitting ideal I_Z=a_N^*I_e (II.1). By Section 9, Z->S is smooth of relative dimension 2, and B=Conf_6(C/S)->S is smooth of relative dimension 6 (an open subscheme of the six-fold fibre power of a smooth relative curve). A closed immersion between two schemes smooth over a common base is a regular immersion, its conormal sheaf is locally free of rank equal to the difference of the relative dimensions, and the conormal sequence is exact and locally split. Hence Z->B is a regular immersion of pure codimension 6-2=4, I_Z/I_Z^2 is locally free of rank 4, and 0->I_Z/I_Z^2->Omega_{B/S}|_Z->Omega_{Z/S}->0 is exact and locally split. This proves (III.2).

Two recorded constraints are relevant and are respected. First, one may not infer lci, regularity, purity or Gysin applicability from the excess numerology 6-4=2 or from its equality with h^1(L): the proof above uses none of that, only smoothness of the two S-schemes. Second, one may not infer from expected codimension 6 versus observed codimension 4 that Z is NOWHERE cut out by a regular sequence: no such conclusion is drawn; on the contrary, the regular-sequence conclusion here is positive, of length 4, and it is compatible with the natural presentation by six equations (a_N^*I_e is generated by the pullbacks of six local generators of the codimension-six ideal I_e of the identity section of the abelian scheme Pic^0), which is exactly the situation the constraint contemplates. Nothing here is asserted about the pair (M_{6,6},Z).

## 11. Part (III.3): the excess bundle, with the tautological twist retained

On B the divisor Gamma is a disjoint union of six sections, so O_Gamma(Gamma) is the direct sum of the normal bundles of those sections and T_{B/S}=pi_*O_Gamma(Gamma) canonically. Pushing forward 0->O_C->O_C(Gamma)->O_Gamma(Gamma)->0 and using R^1pi_*O_Gamma(Gamma)=0 (Gamma is finite over B) gives the globally exact sequence on B

  pi_*O_C(Gamma) -> T_{B/S} --delta--> R^1pi_*O_C -> R^1pi_*O_C(Gamma) -> 0,

so coker(delta)=R^1pi_*O_C(Gamma) and ker(delta)=image(pi_*O_C(Gamma)->pi_*O_Gamma(Gamma)). The map delta is the relative Abel-Jacobi derivative.

Restrict to Z. There O(Gamma) is isomorphic to L tensor pi^*M_univ, so by the projection formula coker(delta)|_Z = R^1pi_*(L tensor pi^*M_univ) = (R^1pi_*L) tensor M_univ, which is locally free of rank 2 by Section 9. The tautological line M_univ is genuinely present and is not trivialized: geometric fibres become abstractly isomorphic to H^1(L) only after choosing a trivialization of the one-dimensional fibre of M_univ, and any downstream Chern-class or excess computation must retain this twist. Set Exc:=coker(delta)|_Z.

Since Exc is locally free of rank 2 and is a quotient of the rank-6 bundle (R^1pi_*O_C)|_Z, the image of delta|_Z is locally free of rank 4 and ker(delta)|_Z is locally free of rank 2. On a geometric fibre, ker(delta) at a point Gamma of Z is the image of H^0(O_C(Gamma)) in H^0(O_Gamma(Gamma)), which is precisely the classical tangent space at Gamma to the Abel-Jacobi fibre |L| inside Sym^6, hence, pulled back along the etale ordering cover of Section 9, precisely the tangent space to the fibre of Z->S. Therefore the composite T_{Z/S} -> T_{B/S}|_Z -> (R^1pi_*O_C)|_Z is a map of vector bundles vanishing on every geometric fibre; Z is reduced (smooth over the reduced S), so that map is zero and T_{Z/S} is contained in ker(delta)|_Z. Both are locally free of rank 2, T_{Z/S} is a subbundle of T_{B/S}|_Z with locally free quotient (Section 10), so the quotient of ker(delta)|_Z by T_{Z/S} is a torsion subsheaf of the locally free sheaf N_{Z/B}, hence zero. This gives the exact sequence

  0 -> T_{Z/S} -> T_{B/S}|_Z -> (R^1pi_*O_C)|_Z -> Exc -> 0

with the ranks 2, 6, 6, 2, so that N_{Z/B}=T_{B/S}|_Z/T_{Z/S} embeds in (R^1pi_*O_C)|_Z as a subbundle of rank 4 with quotient Exc. Dualizing the resulting short exact sequence of bundles and using relative duality ((R^1pi_*O_C)^vee = pi_*omega_{C/S} and (R^1pi_*L)^vee = pi_*(omega_{C/S} tensor L^vee), both locally free of the stated ranks with base change over the reduced S) gives

  0 -> Exc^vee -> (pi_*omega_{C/S})|_Z -> I_Z/I_Z^2 -> 0,  Exc^vee = pi_*(omega_{C/S} tensor L^vee) tensor M_univ^{-1}.

By (I.1) omega_C tensor L^vee = O_C(D) on each geometric fibre, so the fibres of Exc^vee are the two-dimensional spaces H^0(C,O_C(D)) defining the tetragonal pencils (up to the M_univ twist), and the conormal sheaf of Z is the corresponding rank-four quotient of the Hodge bundle. All maps used are canonical and defined directly on Z over S; where a Picard scheme is convenient (for instance to read delta as the derivative of a classifying morphism) one may pass to a base change over which C->S acquires a section, and the canonical sequences descend. This proves (III.3), and it is the local conormal computation that the recorded constraint on excess numerology demands in place of the blocked inference.

## 12. Scope, and what is deliberately not claimed

Proved above: the normalization consequence L=omega_C(-D); non-hyperellipticity of every balanced fibre; constancy h^0(L)=3 with h^1(L)=2 on the whole balanced locus satisfying (N); the degree bound on the fixed part of |L|; existence of a reduced member and density of the reduced-support open on every balanced fibre, with the discriminant of dimension exactly one; nonemptiness, smoothness and the S_6-torsor structure of the ordered fibre incidence; the complete minor-ideal table I_j=O_B for j<=11 and I_12=Fit_0=a_N^*I_e; the identification of Z with the ordered cover of the reduced-support open of a P2-bundle over any reduced base, with smoothness, surjectivity and relative dimension 2; the regular immersion of codimension 4 with locally free conormal of rank 4; and the excess sequence with the twisted identification of coker of the Abel-Jacobi differential.

Not claimed, and not implied by anything above: any statement about unbalanced CE splitting types; any statement about h^0-jumping strata (they do not occur on the balanced locus under (N), which is what is proved, but nothing is asserted about the boundary of that locus); any local-freeness, projective-bundle, smoothness, regular-immersion or excess statement over a nonreduced base; whether L is base-point-free on the balanced locus; any statement about the image, closure, components, stabilizers, purity, codimension, lci status or Gysin/localization behaviour of the corresponding locus in M_{6,6}; and any Hodge, weight, purity or Tate conclusion whatsoever. (N) remains an explicit hypothesis of the theorem, not an established fact, and every clause depending on it is stated under it.

claims.justification: Section 2: SRC-0004 gives deg(O_X(1)|_C)=2g-2+8=18, while (N) gives degree 18+4deg(A); hence deg(A)=0 and Pic(P1)=Z forces A trivial. Substitution into W_f=(O_X(2) tensor gamma^*O(-f))|_C gives the three identities; Riemann-Roch gives chi(L)=1.
claims.statement: Under (CE), (BAL) and (N), on every geometric fibre the residual twist A is trivial, so W_4=omega_C^2, W_5=omega_C^2(-D), L=omega_C(-D), deg(W_4)=20, deg(W_5)=16, deg(L)=6 and chi(L)=1.

claims.justification: Section 3: a hyperelliptic C forces gamma=q o h by the bidegree/arithmetic-genus argument in P1 x P1; then gamma_*O_C=O+O(-1)+O(-4)^2 and E=O(1)+O(4)^2. Tensoring the CE resolution by O_X(2) and using Rp_*O_X(-2)=0 gives 0->F->Sym^2E->gamma_*(O_X(2)|_C)->0; twisting by O(-6) and counting sections (9 versus 7) forces h^0(F(-6))>=2, contradicting F(-6)=O(-2)+O(-1).
claims.statement: Under (CE) and (BAL) alone, no balanced geometric fibre is hyperelliptic.

claims.justification: Section 4: h^0(D)>=2 from gamma^*; Riemann-Roch gives h^0(L)=h^0(D)+1; chi(L)=1 makes D special, so Clifford gives h^0(D)<=3 with equality only in the excluded cases (D=0, D=K by degree; hyperelliptic by CLM-0088-2). The projection formula h^0(D)=2+h^0(E^vee(1)) then forces h^0(E^vee(1))=0.
claims.statement: Under (CE), (BAL) and (N), every balanced geometric fibre has h^0(O_C(D))=2, h^0(L)=3 and h^1(L)=2, so |L| is a projective plane and h^0(L) does not jump on the balanced locus; moreover every summand of E has degree at least two.

claims.justification: Section 5: if the fixed part had degree at least two the moving part would be a base-point-free special g^2_{<=4}; Clifford forces degree exactly 4 with equality, hence C hyperelliptic, contradicting CLM-0088-2.
claims.statement: On every balanced geometric fibre satisfying (N), the fixed part of |L| has degree at most one, hence is reduced, and the moving part is base-point-free of degree 5 or 6 with exactly three sections.

claims.justification: Sections 6-7: the two-jet incidence over the base-point-free moving part has dimension at most one (fibres are points off the finite ramification locus and at most P1 on it), so its closed image misses a dense open of the plane |A|; removing in addition the hyperplane through the at most one fixed point yields a reduced member. Every point of C carries a non-reduced member since h^0(L(-2q))>=1, and pr_2 has finite fibres, so the discriminant has dimension exactly one. Ordering a reduced universal divisor is a free finite etale S_6-action.
claims.statement: On every balanced geometric fibre satisfying (N), |L| contains a divisor of six pairwise distinct points; the non-reduced locus is closed of dimension exactly one; the reduced-support open is nonempty, dense, of dimension two and not closed in |L|; and the ordered incidence in Conf_6(C) is nonempty, smooth of pure dimension two, and a finite etale S_6-torsor of degree 720 over the reduced-support open.

claims.justification: Section 8: ranks and local freeness from CLM-0065-1 with d_4=20, d_5=16, n=6; corank at most one because coker(phi)=coker(phi_5)=R^1pi_*(W_5(-Gamma)) (CLM-0065-3) has fibres Serre-dual to H^0 of a degree-zero line bundle, which is at most one-dimensional; empty vanishing locus of I_11 gives I_11=O_B and hence I_j=O_B for j<=11; the Fitting identity is CLM-0065-4 and CLM-0065-9, whose disjoint-sections hypothesis holds exactly on the ordered configuration base.
claims.statement: Over B=Conf_6(C/S) with its six tautological disjoint sections, pi_*W and pi_*(W|Gamma) are locally free of ranks 26 and 12, every geometric fibre of phi has rank 11 or 12, I_j(phi)=O_B for every j<=11, and I_12(phi)=Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e with formation commuting with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change.

claims.justification: Section 8 with CLM-0088-3 and CLM-0088-5: (26-11)(12-11)=15, (11-5)(6-5)=6, fibre dimension 2 inside relative dimension 6, and h^1(L)=2. Recorded as bookkeeping only; no regularity, depth, lci or Gysin conclusion is drawn from these numbers anywhere in this artifact.
claims.statement: The corank-one locus of the 26-to-12 evaluation has naive determinantal expectation 15 and filtered 11-to-6 expectation 6, while its actual fibres over the balanced locus have pure dimension 2, i.e. codimension 4 in the fibres of Conf_6(C/S)->S; the excess relative to the filtered expectation is 6-4=2=h^1(L).

claims.justification: Section 9: constancy h^0(L)=3 (CLM-0088-3) plus Grauert on a reduced base; the divisor functor of the projective bundle matches the T-point criterion of CLM-0065-4, giving Z = Ord(U) functorially; fibrewise density of the reduced-support open (CLM-0088-5) gives surjectivity of U->S; flatness plus going-down and the dimension formula for flat finite-type morphisms give the component statement. Ordering is applied to the same (unreduced) scheme on both sides, so no reduce-one-side torsor error occurs.
claims.statement: Over a reduced locally Noetherian base, pi_*L is locally free of rank three, AJ=P_S(pi_*L) is a Zariski-locally trivial P2-bundle whose etale locus U is S-smooth of relative dimension two and surjective onto S, and Z is canonically isomorphic to the S_6-torsor of orderings of the universal divisor over U; hence Z->S is smooth surjective of pure relative dimension two, and over a finite-type base every component of Z and of U dominates a component of S with dimension equal to that of the dominated component plus two.

claims.justification: Section 10: Z is closed by the Fitting presentation (CLM-0088-6); Z->S and Conf_6(C/S)->S are smooth of relative dimensions two and six (CLM-0088-8); a closed immersion of schemes smooth over a common base is regular with locally free conormal of rank equal to the difference. No inference is made from the expected-versus-actual codimension comparison, and no nowhere-lci conclusion is drawn.
claims.statement: Over a reduced base, the closed immersion Z->Conf_6(C/S) is a regular immersion of pure codimension four, its conormal sheaf is locally free of rank four, and the conormal sequence is exact and locally split.

claims.justification: Section 11: T_{B/S}=pi_*O_Gamma(Gamma) for disjoint sections; the pushforward of 0->O_C->O_C(Gamma)->O_Gamma(Gamma)->0 gives coker(delta)=R^1pi_*O(Gamma), which on Z is (R^1pi_*L) tensor M_univ by the projection formula; the classical identification of ker(delta) with the tangent space to the Abel-Jacobi fibre, together with reducedness of Z and a torsion-in-a-bundle argument, identifies ker(delta)|_Z with T_{Z/S}; relative duality dualizes the sequence. The tautological twist M_univ is retained and not trivialized.
claims.statement: Over a reduced base there is a canonical exact sequence 0->T_{Z/S}->T_{B/S}|_Z->(R^1pi_*O_C)|_Z->Exc->0 on Z with Exc=coker of the relative Abel-Jacobi differential canonically isomorphic to (R^1pi_*L) tensor M_univ, locally free of rank two; dually 0->Exc^vee->(pi_*omega_{C/S})|_Z->I_Z/I_Z^2->0 with Exc^vee=pi_*(omega_{C/S} tensor L^vee) tensor M_univ^{-1}, whose fibres are the two-dimensional spaces of the tetragonal pencils.

novelty_claims: Fibrewise nonemptiness of the reduced-support open of |L|, hence of the ordered Conf_6 incidence, is proved on EVERY balanced geometric fibre without assuming that L is base-point-free: the fixed part is bounded in degree by Clifford (hence is reduced) and the moving part is handled by a two-jet incidence count. The working context records the available route as requiring base-point-freeness plus Bertini; that hypothesis is removed, so the conclusion is insensitive to whether base points occur on the balanced locus.

Constancy h^0(L)=3 on the whole balanced locus is derived from balancedness itself: Clifford equality in the h^0(D)=3 case forces hyperellipticity, and a hyperelliptic degree-four cover has h^0(F(-6))>=2, contradicting F=O(4)+O(5). This supplies precisely the missing hypothesis that blocks the relative P2-bundle model over balanced tetragonal moduli, and it does so using only the hyperelliptic exclusion, not any claim about non-primitive pencils through positive-genus intermediate curves.

The local complete-intersection question is settled positively and by the right method: Z is a regular closed immersion of codimension four in Conf_6(C/S) with locally free conormal of rank four, proved from S-smoothness of both schemes rather than from the blocked expected-versus-actual codimension numerology, and accompanied by the explicit conormal sequence that the recorded constraint demands.

The excess of the CE rank-drop presentation is computed as a bundle, not a number: coker of the relative Abel-Jacobi differential on Z is canonically (R^1pi_*L) tensor M_univ of rank two, with the convention-dependent tautological twist retained, and its dual is the rank-two bundle whose fibres are the tetragonal pencils H^0(O_C(D)); the conormal sheaf of Z appears as the corresponding rank-four quotient of the Hodge bundle.

The minor-ideal table for the CE evaluation is completed on the ordered configuration base, where the ATT-0065 disjoint-sections hypothesis is actually satisfied: I_j(phi)=O_B for every j<=11 and I_12(phi)=Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e, with no claim for an arbitrary relative degree-six divisor.
summary: Computation-lane lemma for C66-COMP-RANK. Under (CE)+(BAL)+(N) it proves that on EVERY balanced geometric fibre h^0(L)=3 without jumping, that the fixed part of |L| has degree at most one, and that |L| contains a reduced divisor, so the reduced-support open is dense and the ordered Conf_6 incidence is nonempty, smooth of pure dimension two: this discharges the packet frontier obligation on fibrewise nonemptiness, and does so WITHOUT assuming L base-point-free, by killing the fixed part with Clifford and treating the moving part with a two-jet incidence count. The minor-ideal table of the CE evaluation is completed: I_j(phi)=O_B for all j<=11 and I_12(phi)=Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e (the last imported from the twice-confirmed ATT-0065, whose six-disjoint-sections hypothesis is exactly met on the ordered configuration base). Over a reduced base the rank-drop scheme Z is identified with the S_6-torsor of orderings over the reduced-support open of the P2-bundle P_S(pi_*L), hence is smooth and surjective over S of relative dimension two, and is regularly embedded in Conf_6(C/S) with codimension four and locally free conormal of rank four; the excess is computed as coker of the Abel-Jacobi differential, canonically (R^1pi_*L) tensor M_univ with the tautological twist retained. The lci and excess conclusions are obtained from smoothness and an explicit conormal computation, not from the blocked expected-versus-actual codimension numerology.

theorem_scope.base: algebraically closed field of characteristic zero; S locally Noetherian for Parts I-II; Part III additionally assumes S reduced, and the component-dimension formula in (III.1) additionally assumes S of finite type over k. Statements over an algebraic stack hold on a smooth atlas and descend, since every construction used (Grauert local freeness on a reduced base, Sym^6 and Conf_6, projectivization, Fitting ideals, relative duality) is smooth-local on the base.
theorem_scope.generality: Part II (rank strata and minor ideals) uses only (CE), (BAL) and the ATT-0065 hypotheses; Parts I and III use (N) in addition. Gamma is always the universal divisor of six pairwise-disjoint tautological sections, i.e. the base is the ordered configuration space, which is exactly where the ATT-0065 disjoint-section hypothesis holds; no statement is made for an arbitrary relative degree-six divisor. The Clifford and jet-incidence arguments of Part I are specific to (g,deg L)=(6,6); the determinantal and excess bookkeeping of Parts II-III is written so that only the stated degree inequalities are used.
theorem_scope.hypotheses: (CE) standard degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl ideal resolution, exactly as in the ATT-0065 theorem hypotheses; (BAL) fibrewise F = O(4)+O(5); (N) fibrewise CE relative-canonical normalization O_X(1)|_C = omega_{C/P1} tensor gamma^*A. (N) is carried as an explicit hypothesis throughout and is never asserted; it is the packet's undischarged relative-canonical normalization, and every clause depending on it is stated under it rather than gap-marked.
theorem_scope.not_covered: unbalanced CE splitting types; h^0-jumping strata; nonreduced bases in Part III (no local freeness, projective-bundle, smoothness, regular-immersion or excess claim is made there); base-point-freeness of L on the balanced locus, which is neither asserted nor denied; images, closure, components, stabilizers, purity, codimension, lci status or Gysin/localization for the pair (M_{6,6},Z); the classifying map to M_{6,6} and its injectivity or stabilizers; any Hodge, weight, purity or Tate conclusion; characteristic p; integral coefficients and coarse-space statements.

theorem_statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, S a locally Noetherian k-scheme, pi:C->S smooth and proper with geometrically connected genus-six fibres, s:P->S a P1-bundle, gamma:C->P finite flat of degree four with Tschirnhausen bundle E (gamma_*O_C = O_P direct-sum E^vee, E of rank three), p:X=P_P(E^vee)->P the associated P2-bundle in the packet convention p_*O_X(1)=E, i:C->X the Casnati-Ekedahl embedding, and F a rank-two bundle on P. Assume: (CE) the ideal of i has the standard degree-four CE resolution 0->O_X(-4) tensor p^*det(F)->O_X(-2) tensor p^*F->I_C->0; (BAL) F restricted to every geometric fibre of s is O(4) direct-sum O(5); (N) on every geometric fibre, O_X(1)|_C is isomorphic to omega_{C/P1} tensor gamma^*A for some A in Pic(P1). Put W=i^*(O_X(2) tensor p^*F^vee) with the canonical filtration 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 induced by the O(5)-subbundle of F, L=W_5 tensor omega_{C/S}^{-1}, D=gamma^*O_P(1); O_P(1), hence W_4,W_5,L,D, is well defined only up to twist by a line bundle pulled back from S, and every assertion below is invariant under such a twist. THEN: (I) On every geometric fibre: (I.1) A is trivial, W_5=omega_C^{tensor 2}(-D), L=omega_C(-D), deg(L)=6, chi(L)=1, deg(W_4)=20, deg(W_5)=16; (I.2) C is not hyperelliptic; (I.3) h^0(O_C(D))=2, h^0(L)=3, h^1(L)=2, so |L| is a projective plane, and every summand of E has degree at least two; (I.4) the fixed part of |L| has degree at most one, hence is reduced, and the moving part is base-point-free with three sections; (I.5) the non-reduced locus Delta in |L| is closed of dimension exactly one, so the reduced-support locus |L|^red = |L| minus Delta is a nonempty dense open subset of dimension two and is not closed in |L|; (I.6) the ordered incidence {(p_1,...,p_6) in C^6 pairwise distinct with p_1+...+p_6 in |L|} is nonempty, smooth of pure dimension two, and a finite etale S_6-torsor of degree 720 over |L|^red. (II) Let B=Conf_6(C/S) be the complement of the big diagonal in the six-fold fibre product, with its six tautological pairwise-disjoint sections, universal divisor Gamma, evaluation phi:pi_*W->pi_*(W|Gamma), N=omega_{C/S} tensor W_5^vee(Gamma), a_N:B->Pic^0_{C_B/B} and identity section e. Then pi_*W and pi_*(W|Gamma) are locally free of ranks 26 and 12, every geometric fibre of phi has rank 11 or 12, and: (II.1) I_j(phi)=O_B for every j<=11, while I_12(phi)=Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e cuts out the closed subscheme Z=a_N^{-1}(e(B)), whose formation commutes with arbitrary locally Noetherian base change; (II.2) the naive maximal-minor expectation for a 26-to-12 map is codimension 15 and the filtered 11-to-6 expectation is codimension 6, whereas the geometric fibres of Z->S have pure dimension two, i.e. codimension four in the fibres of B->S, the excess being 6-4=2=h^1(L). (III) Assume in addition S reduced. Then pi_*L is locally free of rank three, AJ=P_S(pi_*L) is a Zariski-locally trivial P2-bundle carrying a universal relative degree-six divisor, its etale locus U (the reduced-support open) is S-smooth of pure relative dimension two and surjective onto S, and the S_6-torsor of orderings of the universal divisor over U is canonically isomorphic to Z. Consequently: (III.1) Z->S is smooth and surjective of pure relative dimension two; if moreover S is of finite type over k, every irreducible component of Z and of U dominates an irreducible component of S and has dimension equal to the dimension of that component plus two; (III.2) the closed immersion Z->B is a regular immersion of pure codimension four, its conormal sheaf I_Z/I_Z^2 is locally free of rank four, and the conormal sequence 0->I_Z/I_Z^2->Omega_{B/S}|_Z->Omega_{Z/S}->0 is exact and locally split; (III.3) with delta:T_{B/S}=pi_*O_Gamma(Gamma)->R^1pi_*O_C the connecting map of 0->O_C->O_C(Gamma)->O_Gamma(Gamma)->0, the sequence 0->T_{Z/S}->T_{B/S}|_Z->(R^1pi_*O_C)|_Z->Exc->0 is exact on Z with Exc=coker(delta)|_Z canonically isomorphic to (R^1pi_*L) tensor M_univ, locally free of rank two, where M_univ is the tautological line bundle on Z determined by O(Gamma)=L tensor pi^*M_univ; dually 0->Exc^vee->(pi_*omega_{C/S})|_Z->I_Z/I_Z^2->0 is exact with Exc^vee = pi_*(omega_{C/S} tensor L^vee) tensor M_univ^{-1}, whose fibres are the two-dimensional spaces H^0(C,O_C(D)) of the tetragonal pencils. No assertion is made about images, closure, components, stabilizers, purity, codimension or Gysin maps in M_{6,6}, about unbalanced splitting types or h^0-jumping strata, about nonreduced bases in Part III, or about Hodge, weight or Tate type.
